en: The Department of Health runs a national immunization program to protect Filipino children from preventable diseases like measles and polio through free vaccines.
After the 1991 Mount Pinatubo eruption, the government built massive lahar dams to protect nearby communities from deadly mudflows during heavy rains.
The Ifugao people maintain the muyong forest canopy above their rice terraces to prevent soil erosion and ensure a clean, steady water supply.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator that uses hot water bottles to safely keep premature babies warm in rural areas without electricity.
The Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004 legally protects rivers from industrial pollution to ensure communities have access to safe, clean drinking water.
During the Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate homes with kiping made from dyed rice leaves, promoting biodegradable materials instead of harmful, non-degradable plastics.
The Philippine Red Cross trains citizens in basic first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation to save lives during medical emergencies and natural disasters.
The T'boli people extract natural dyes from local plants to color their t'nalak cloth, avoiding the toxic chemicals found in synthetic fabric dyes.
The Office of Civil Defense coordinates disaster preparedness drills to protect Filipinos from the physical dangers of typhoons, earthquakes, and fires.
The Philippine carabao wallows in mud to lower its body temperature and protect its sensitive skin from severe sunburns and biting insects.
National Scientist Gregorio Zara invented the alcohol stove, providing households with a safe, smokeless cooking method that reduces indoor air pollution and respiratory illnesses.
The Department of Health scientifically validates traditional medicinal plants like oregano and lagundi to safely treat coughs and asthma in local clinics.
